# Media Foundation Gotchas

> Known Media Foundation / IMFTransform patterns that cause silent failures or hard-to-debug errors. Applies to any language driving MFTs, including hand-written COM vtable calls from Go, Rust or C# where the SDK headers are not available to transcribe from.

## Entries

- [MFT_MESSAGE_NOTIFY_END_OF_STREAM comes before START_OF_STREAM in the enum, and transposing them silently stalls every async MFT](mft-stream-notify-constants-transposed.md): END_OF_STREAM is 0x10000002 and START_OF_STREAM is 0x10000003, the opposite order to how anyone says them; transposed, a synchronous MFT keeps working perfectly while an asynchronous one accepts every media type, returns an event generator, and then never queues METransformNeedInput -- ProcessInput returns MF_E_NOTACCEPTING forever with no error anywhere, which reads as a vendor driver quirk. The working software path is the strongest false signal that your code is fine. HIGH.
- [A hardware encoder MFT will not accept a media type at all until you give it a Direct3D device](hardware-mft-needs-d3d-manager.md): MFT_MESSAGE_SET_D3D_MANAGER is a precondition for configuration, not a GPU-residency optimisation, for any transform advertising MF_SA_D3D11_AWARE. Each vendor fails differently -- AMD returns MF_E_TRANSFORM_TYPE_NOT_SET in both type orders (sending you off swapping input/output order, which is not the problem), Microsoft's DX12 encoder returns 0x80041000, and NVIDIA's configures cleanly and then silently never asks for a frame. Also: enumerate and try every candidate, since the first is not always usable. HIGH.
- [Rebuilding an MFT leaks it unless you close the old one first, and "first" means nothing without a lock](mft-rebuild-close-and-serialize.md): settings baked into the media type force a rebuild rather than a live adjustment, and the rebuild goes wrong twice. Assigning over the encoder pointer drops the last reference without releasing the COM object, so the transform, its activation object and its driving thread leak per rebuild with no error and no failed frame -- the picture stays correct and the only symptom is a session that degrades the more the user touches the setting. Then adding the missing Close introduces a race, because setting the pointer nil is exactly what a capture loop on another thread reads as "build one", so both threads construct a transform at once on the one shared ID3D11Device: the overlap the ordering was chosen to avoid, reached from the other direction. Fixing either half alone produces the other. HIGH.
- [MF_MT_MAX_KEYFRAME_SPACING counts submitted frames, so "two seconds" becomes a minute on a still screen](keyframe-spacing-counts-frames.md): The attribute is a frame COUNT, and the usual `interval/1s * frameRate` conversion is correct only while frames are actually submitted at that rate. Desktop capture is variable rate by nature (DXGI reports presents, not pixels, so a still screen is fed by a ~1fps repaint floor), and 60 frames then means 60 seconds rather than 2. A session against a kiosk or POS terminal therefore contains exactly one keyframe, at the start, and a receiver that misses any fragment of that opening IDR is black for the rest of the call with both ends reporting health. No frame count fixes it: small enough for 1fps destroys the bitrate at 30fps. Add a wall-clock keyframe floor, and force one by reconfiguring the encoder with the config it already has, since a rebuilt pipeline's first sample is an IDR with parameter sets. HIGH.
